r3_neural_time_arms.setup: FD002 208 train / 52 val engines, window 50, cap 125, replication of official builder verified True
r3_neural_time_arms.finding: removing the time feature improves held-out RMSE by ~1.36 (3/3 seeds) and lowers NASA mean; late rises 0.269->0.282
r3_neural_time_arms.caveat: simplified preprocessing (no OperatingConditionScaler); absolute level not comparable to the frozen pipeline (40.86)
r3_neural_time_arms.next: replicate on the frozen pipeline with an add-only config

r3_frozen_cycle_test.probe_refuted: the simplified probe said removing cycle helps (-1.36); it used only 208 training windows vs thousands in the frozen pipeline
r3_frozen_cycle_test.mechanism: cycle benefit concentrates on long-lived engines (5.31) and is small for short-lived (1.61); short-lived engines are over-predicted by +7 to +11 in both variants
r3_frozen_cycle_test.next_hypothesis: normalise time by an estimated own-lifespan scale c/T_hat; may keep long-life benefit while cutting short-life over-prediction

r3_scale.deployable_estimator: degenerate: 0 of 154 windows yield a finite unclipped estimate; 60% NaN (slope<=0), 40% clipped at the lower bound
r3_scale.conclusion: the oracle gain is NOT reachable via a better time feature; the bottleneck is that the observable health index is not monotone
r3_scale.next_hypothesis: build a monotone multi-sensor health index (condition-corrected FPCA-style) and test whether prefix extrapolation becomes usable
r3_scale.falsifiable: if monotonicity on held-out engines stays below ~0.3, the extrapolation will still degenerate

r3_four_arms_retracted.mechanism: the estimated scale fixes mid and long lifespan cases; the unrealised 5.1 RMSE sits entirely in short-lived engines, which every arm over-predicts by +10 to +16
r3_four_arms_retracted.hypothesis: the single-constant failure level L causes T_hat to be too large for fast-degrading units; stratifying L by condition cluster or degradation rate should shrink that bias
caveats: probe setting (no OperatingConditionScaler), absolute level not comparable
late and severe do NOT improve -> no safety claim
relative to the cycle arm, not to a strong baseline

r3_1_four_arms.setting: FD002 208 train / 52 held-out engines, one matched cutoff per engine, 30 epochs, seeds 2027-2029, ~32k training windows, CandidateModel 41,858 params, probe preprocessing (no OperatingConditionScaler)

paired_engine_clustered_bootstrap._format: [delta_rmse, ci_lo, ci_hi, excludes_zero]; positive = first arm better

verdict: deployable per-engine scale normalisation has NO detectable gain over cycle (+0.08, CI crosses 0) and is not better than the constant-median arm (pooled 20.15)
the only significant effects are oracle (+8.23) and the leak itself (-2.78); the previously reported 38% was produced by leakage
the headroom direction (lifespan scale) survives; the current health-index/prefix estimator does not
r3_1_four_arms.gate_for_reuse: do not feed T_hat into any candidate or the frozen pipeline until corr(T_hat, T_true) >= 0.5 on held-out engines
